sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 9:8

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 9:8:1
items.html: A further rule also emerges for us: no MAN [Mayin Nukvin] avail and are detained there except two times — one, the first time, when they rose; and two, the second time, when they were depicted: That is, as said in the adjacent item: at the first time they rise with the Katnut of the upper to the upper of the upper, and there they are not yet depicted; and at the second time a special coupling is made for them in their upper, and then their Katnut is depicted; and afterwards they descend to their place. And in those two times, the MAN [Mayin Nukvin] of Katnut are completed entirely, and they need no further rising or correction for themselves. Rather, at the time of Gadlut they certainly rise a second time as MAN; however, the MAN of Gadlut are not those MAN of Katnut, but they are other MAN that the Partzuf raises to its upper; but the earlier MAN of Katnut are already completed, and they no longer need rising. And this is the second rule here.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 9:8:2
items.html:
Firstborn sons, like, for example, ZON [Zeir Anpin and Nukva] to AVI [Aba ve Ima], being their firstborn MAN, are never absent from there, and it is impossible for any MAN to rise, etc., except by means of them: Explanation: there are always two discernments in MAN [Mayin Nukvin]: the first is the discernment of the posterior of the upper that fell to the degree of the lower; and the second is the degree of the lower itself, as said above. Also you know that although both of them rise together as MAN to the upper, nevertheless the degree of the lower included in the MAN — which has now risen at the first time as MAN — is not corrected there in that coupling with the upper; rather, it needs a second coupling, as above. And therefore the lights that were clothed in those two discernments are regarded as brothers to one another, for in their source, before the rising of MAN, the two discernments were only one discernment in the degree of the lower, as above. But from the discernment of their birth they separated from one another, for they came out in two couplings, one after the other: the posterior of the upper in the MAN came out in the upper of the upper and were completed there; and the anterior vessels of the lower came out and were completed in their upper, as above. Hence the first discernment is regarded as the firstborn son, and the second discernment is regarded as his second brother.
And this matter is practiced in all the kinds of MAN in the worlds. For this is the rule: the posterior of the upper, which are AHP, are always found in the anterior vessels of the lower, which are GE — for the AHP of the lower also fell to the degree lower than them, and nothing remained in it but GE alone. And in the same manner in all the degrees: all kinds of MAN necessarily have in them two discernments — the posterior of the upper and the anterior of the lower — except that they are considered one discernment of MAN, because both are in one degree, for the upper that descends to the place of the lower becomes like it. And likewise, at the time of the rising of the MAN from any discernment whatsoever, it is also regarded that the anterior of the lower rise together with the posterior of the upper within it, to the upper of the upper, namely to the third degree, as above; and it is also regarded then that the two are included in one another at the time of the coupling, except that the anterior of the lower becomes there the externality upon the posterior of the upper. And since the externality of the MAN is not yet depicted in that coupling in the upper of the upper, but descends from there with its own posterior of the upper, which have already received all their correction, and the coupling is made upon it in its own upper, the one adjacent to it, as above — therefore, after they receive their correction and their lights, those two discernments in the MAN are regarded as brothers to one another: the posterior of the upper is regarded as the firstborn brother, and the anterior of the lower is regarded as his second brother.
And this is what he said: “however, their first MAN, which were in the world, each and every one in its place, in the secret of firstborn sons — as, for example, ZON to AVI, being their firstborn sons — are never absent from there.” That is, as explained: those MAN that rose with AVI to AA for the sake of the Gadlut of AVI are composed of two discernments — of the posterior of AVI and of the anterior vessels of ZON — and the coupling is made upon both together; however, from this coupling in AA only the posterior of AVI were depicted, and the anterior of ZON are not corrected in this coupling, but descend with AVI below, where a second coupling is then made in AVI, and there the anterior vessels of ZON are corrected, namely their GE, which are the discernment of the Katnut of ZON. And therefore the lights and the vessels in the posterior of AVI are regarded as firstborn brothers to ZON, because these posterior were in one degree with ZON — both before the coupling of the Gadlut of AVI and at the time when the coupling was made upon them in AA for the sake of the Gadlut of AVI, as above — except that since they were corrected in the first coupling, in AA, they are regarded as firstborn to ZON, which were corrected afterwards through the second coupling. And you should understand, however, that the intention is not the GAR [first three] of AVI, for ZON were never in one degree with them; rather, the intention is only the AHP of AVI, which are called the posterior of AVI.
And this is what he said, “they are never absent from there”: for these posterior of AVI joined in the building of the Partzuf of AVI itself, and therefore they cannot be absent from there. Not so the anterior of ZON: although they were attached together to these posterior of AVI, nevertheless, after the above second coupling, they separate from the posterior of AVI and come out from there to their place below, for they were recognized as being not of the discernment of AVI but of the degree of ZON; and this is the secret of the birth.
And this is what he said, “and it is impossible for any MAN to rise from there onward, etc., except by means of them”: for every degree that comes into ZON must repeat all the ways practiced in their first Azilut of ZON, for there is no renewal of illumination but from Ein Sof; and therefore all the Partzufim must raise MAN to one another up to Ein Sof, and then new light descends to them from Ein Sof, in the secret of MAD to AK and through all the degrees, in the same order in which they were first emanated, until the Mochin come to ZON. And therefore the ARI says that the new MAN and MAD bestowed to ZON from AVI bestow nothing except by means of the above posterior of AVI, which are the firstborn brothers of ZON; for since they are in great proximity to ZON, they raise the MAN of ZON to AVI for the sake of their Mochin. And without them, ZON would not be able to rise to AVI, which is above their degree — as is known, no degree can rise above its own degree.
